text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGEREF: Multi-GPU collective stall detected in cluster `dedicated-west-3`. Route: /v1/generate (model: gptx-tp4). Error spike 18% over 5m. Suspected: NCCL timeouts + CUDA Xid resets. Pager: @maya @owen

maya: seeing repeating NCCL timeout traces and one node restarting containers. will drop into the node logs now.

ow: copy of recent logs: 
```
[2026-03-15T01:12:23Z] rank 2: NCCL WARN Call to ncclAllReduce timed out after 12000ms
[2026-03-15T01:12:24Z] gpu0 kernel: Xid 79: GPU page fault
[2026-03-15T01:12:24Z] container: exit code 137 (OOM-kill) on container model-server-2
[2026-03-15T01:12:25Z] k8s kubelet: restarting container model-server-2 (backoff)
[2026-03-15T01:12:29Z] nccl_comm: communicator 0x7f9fb... lost peer 3
```

carla: customer-impact flag: small set of customers on Dedicated impacted, one reported timeouts. CS notified.

alex: quick triage: looks like memory pressure on rank 2 causing OOM, triggers container restart and then NCCL communicator fail -> ripple across TP ranks.

maya: taking oncall lead for now. immediate mitigation ideas: 1) cordon + drain the node with repeated restarts, 2) scale down TP degree for affected pool (fallback to DP/1-gpu replica), 3) apply kernel-level cuda watchdog workaround if available.

own: I'm on it. running `kubectl get pods -o wide` and `kubectl describe` on the failing pod.

ow: run commands I'm running:
```bash
kubectl get pods -n redwood-dedicated | grep model-server-2
kubectl logs model-server-2 -n redwood-dedicated --previous\kubectl cordon n-dedicated-43\kubectl drain n-dedicated-43 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force\```

maya: found high RSS on rank 2 process: 86GB on a 96GB GPU host; swap pressure on host, lots of retries from other ranks trying to sync.

carla: CS update to customer (AcmePayments): "We're investigating degraded generation performance and occasional timeouts on your Dedicated cluster. We'll post a status update in 15 minutes." Ticket created: Redwood-INC-2026-435.

eng-ml: this pattern matches previous tensor-parallel stalls where a single rank OOM triggers NCCL retries and eventually communicator hang. Could be a growth in sequence length for a specific tenant workload.

maya: mitigation step 1 complete: cordoned n-dedicated-43 and drained model pods off it. traffic routing config updated to avoid that node.

pagerduty: acknowledgment recorded. Primary oncall: maya. Secondary: owen.

ow: after drain we see residual NCCL errors but no new container restarts for 3m. throughput recovering to ~85% baseline.

alex: suggest immediate config change: enforce max_sequence_length=1024 for that route; limit batch size to 1 for TP jobs for 30m window. Pushing a temporary config patch to the router.

maya: pushed router flag `max_seq:1024`, `tp_batch:1` to canary for the affected customer pool. Observability showing tail latency drop.

eng-ml: recommend capturing KV-cache snapshots for the rollout test and running a repro on staging with high seq lengths.

carla: CS: AcmePayments reports partial recovery but still seeing a 5% error rate on long-context jobs. they want ETA.

maya: quick customer impact summary for ops log: 03/15 01:10-01:32 UTC - degraded throughput and timeouts for Dedicated cluster `dedicated-west-3` affecting AcmePayments. ~12 requests failed definitively, 80 requests experienced >2x latency. No PII exposure.

ow: also seeing repeated kernel Xid 79 on GPU1 before OOM; file created /var/log/nvidia-xid.log attached.

ow: temp fix executed: drained node, router config tightened, autoscaler nudged to spin up 2 spare single-GPU replicas for fallthrough.

own: taking point for next shift. summary for handoff: root symptoms: per-rank memory spike -> OOM kill -> container restart -> NCCL communicator timeouts and hang for TP group. mitigations applied: node drained, route limited, fallback replicas started. follow-ups: RCA, add per-rank memory guard, alert on rising per-rank RSS and seq length, test repro in staging.

own: I'll coordinate with eng-runtime and eng-ml tomorrow, tagging @sre-lead and @eng-ml for RCA ownership.

sre-lead: escalate: create incident page and assign RCA to eng-runtime (primary) and eng-ml (secondary). Include impact metrics and timeline. Postmortem owner: owen.

cs-ops: logged customer update sent at 01:38 UTC. SLA hit? monitoring calculates <minute of complete outage, but latency SLO breached for 22 minutes. recommend outreach to AcmePayments CSM.

eng-ml: quick note — collect the following artifacts: full core dumps from model-server on rank 2 (if available), nvcrash logs, NCCL debug log at level INFO, and the router request trace for the affected request ids.

maya: saved logs to /mnt/incidents/1758004321/artifacts.tar.gz and granted eng runtime access.

incident-bot: created incident record IR-2026-1758004321 and set severity to Sev2. Meeting bridge: #incident-1758004321.

ow: handoff to owen at 01:40 UTC. I'm pausing active remediation; please escalate if a node flaps again.

ow: final quick timeline for handoff message:
- 01:10 UTC: first NCCL timeout observed
- 01:12 UTC: container model-server-2 OOM -> exit 137 -> restart
- 01:13 UTC: NCCL communicator errors escalate, other ranks retry
- 01:15 UTC: node showing GPU Xid 79 errors repeatedly
- 01:22 UTC: cordon + drain executed on n-dedicated-43
- 01:26 UTC: router config updated (max_seq, tp_batch) and fallback replicas created
- 01:32 UTC: error rate dropped to background; residual latency for long-seq jobs remains

ow: owen: acknowledged and took over. I'll run the RCA checklist and coordinate patch.

own: oncall notes saved. next actions assigned: 
- eng-runtime: add per-rank mem guard + alert (owner: alex)
- eng-ml: run repro with increased seqs in staging (owner: eng-ml)
- infra: check for node-level firmware / driver anomalies on n-dedicated-43 (owner: infra-team)
- cs-ops: send follow-up to AcmePayments with incident summary and mitigation steps (owner: carla)

carla: will schedule customer sync if they request deeper post-incident review.

sre-lead: good containment. ensure the postmortem includes timeline, contributing factors, and specific remediation (e.g., memory caps, router guardrails, improved NCCL retry logic).

incident-bot: closing the active page; incident remains open for RCA.

ow: thanks all — handing off fully to owen for RCA and postmortem drafting.
